question: According to statements made by Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó in the media (source), Kaja Kallas supposedly suggested during the EU Foreign Affairs Council meeting on 23 February 2026 that Hungary and Slovakia should send soldiers to Ukraine instead of experts to inspect the damaged Druzhba oil pipeline. Szijjártó described this as a new level of pressure from Brussels1. 1.

Can the Vice-President / High Representative confirm that she suggested that Hungary and Slovakia send soldiers to Ukraine instead of experts to inspect the Druzhba pipeline during the aforementioned Council meeting?
If so, where does she get the authority to make such statements, since the Treaties certainly do not give it to her?

If the above statement was indeed made, then this is an extremely serious matter, as the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs is recommending that Member States act in violation of international law (which sending troops without a UN Security Council mandate certainly would be). Is she therefore considering stepping down from her position as Vice-President / High Representative, given that the person holding that mandate should know and respect international law, rather than call for it to be violated?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.5.2026) Ukraine has successfully repaired and reopened on 23 April 2026 the Druzhba oil pipeline which was previously damaged by Russia’s attacks. Ukraine has therefore restored the flow of crude oil to Hungary and Slovakia. The EU’s priority is to ensure energy security for all European citizens.

That’s why the Commission engaged in intense discussions with Member States and Ukraine at all levels to help restore the flow of oil to Hungary and Slovakia1. The EU also played a role by offering Ukraine technical support and funding. The EU will also continue to work on alternative routes for the transit of non-Russian crude oil to the countries of Central and Eastern Europe.
